sentences.text:
The ACP, Kengeri Sub Division has submitted charge sheet against the accused persons for the offence punishable U/s.498A, 304(B) of IPC in Crime No.10/2018 of Rajarajeshwari Nagar P.S.
2.
The brief story of the prosecution are as under:
The marriage between the son of accused persons by name Vishwanath and deceased Nirmala was performed on 02.11.2016.
After marriage, the deceased started to reside alongwith her husband with her in-laws, i.e. both accused Nos.1 and 2 at Plot No.008, Temple Bells Premier Apartment, situated at R.R.Nagar, Bengaluru.
The husband of the deceased went to the abroad i.e. Japan on job.

During the absence of the husband of the deceased, both accused persons subjected the deceased Smt.Nirmala physically and mentally by demanding additional dowry in terms of cash of RS.20 Lakhs from her parental house for construction of house and also restricted her to visit her parental house.

Due to the continuous physical and mental torture, on 10.01.2018 at her matrimonial home,
the deceased committed suicide by hanging herself and thereby the accused persons have committed the offences as alleged against them.
3. The concerned police have submitted charge sheet before the concerned ACMM., Bangalore.
The learned Magistrate has took cognizance of the offences and committed the case to the Sessions Court by complying Sec.207 of Cr.P.C. after furnishing copy of charge sheet to the accused persons.

The same was numbered as SC No.97/2019.
4.
The prosecution has examined eight witnesses as PW.1 to PW.8 and got exhibited documents at Ex.P1 to P9 and M.Os.1 to 7.
On consent of the accused counsel, the inquest Mahazar and P.M.Report have been marked at Ex.P.6 and 7 respectively.
As such the learned PP gave up the witnesses C.W.5 to C.W.7.
So also the learned PP has given up the witnesses C.W.18 to C.W.22 in view of the evidence of C.W.23 and C.W.24.

The court has issued summons, warrant against C.W.8,
C.W.9, C.W.13 to C.W.17.

Inspite of issue of summons, warrant and proclamation, the police failed to execute warrant and produce them before the court to record their evidence, as such the prayer of the learned PP was rejected and the witnesses C.W.8, C.W.9, C.W.13 to C.W.17 were dropped.

However liberty has been given to the prosecution for examination of the said witnesses, if the said witnesses brought before the court by the concerned police before conclusion of trial.
5.
After completion of prosecution side evidence, this Court has recorded the statement of accused No.2, as provided U/s.313 of Cr.P.C.
The accused No.2 has denied incriminating evidence present against her and not claimed any defense evidence nor submitted anything to the Court.
The accused No.2 has complied application u/s.437A of Cr.PC by executing personal bond and surety bond.

6. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the materials on record.
7.

The following points that arises for consideration of this court:

sentences.text: Whether the prosecution proves that the son of accused persons by name Vishwanath and deceased-Smt.Nirmala are being the husband and wife, the accused No.1(abated) and accused No.2 being the in-laws of Smt.Nirmala, when her husband went abroad, they subjected the deceased to physical and mental cruelty by abusing her in filthy language to bring additional dowry of Rs.20 lakhs to construct the building and thereby accused persons have committed an offence punishable u/s 498A of IPC?

2. Whether the prosecution proves that accused Nos.1 and 2 being the in-laws of deceased Smt.Nirmala, subjected deceased to physical and mental cruelty, due to the continuous physical and mental torture, received by the deceased from the accused persons, on 10.01.2018 at her matrimonial home, the deceased committed suicide by hanging herself and thereby accused persons have committed an offence punishable U/s.304(B) of IPC?
3. What order?
8.

This Court has answered the above above points are as under:
 Point No.1: In the Negative  Point No.2: In the Negative  Point No.3: As per final order  for the following:
 R E A S O N S 9.
Points Nos.1 and 2: These points are taken up together as they are related to each other and to avoid repetition in the discussion.
The prosecution is required to establish the guilt against the accused persons by placing reliable evidence.
In this case, the accused No.1 being the husband of accused No.2 has died during the pendency of trial.
As such, the present case against accused No.1 abated.
In this case, the concerned Investigation Officer has failed to produce the death note and also marriage invitation inspite of directions issued by the court.
As such the prosecution has failed to get mark the said vital document death note.
Apart from that, the documents marriage photos marked at Ex.P.2 clearly establish that the marriage of deceased Nirmala with Vishwanatha was perform on 02.11.2016.
So far as the marriage is concerned, there is no dispute.
So also, the death of the deceased is concerned, the inquest Mahazar and P.M.Report has been marked at Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7.

Such being the case,
whether mere marking of Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7 is enough to believe the allegations made against the accused.

According to this court, it is the burden present on the prosecution to place such evidence to consider due to the continuous physical and mental torture to the deceased with regard to additional dowry as alleged against the accused persons has committed suicide.

sentences.text: It is necessary to note that the father of the deceased, the uncle son of the deceased by name Chethan, brother of the deceased Deepak, the relative of the deceased by name Dayananda have clearly deposed about the marriage between the deceased and Mr.Vishwanatha i.e. son of accused persons.

The evidence also reveals that after marriage, the deceased has started to reside with her husband and accused persons at Plot No.008, Temple Bells Premier Apartment, situated at R.R.Nagar, Bengaluru.

Except that, not elicited any evidence by the prosecution to believe because of the physical and mental torture given by accused persons to bring additional dowry of Rs.20 lakhs by way of cash for construction of the house, the deceased has committed suicide.
It is the say of the father of the deceased by name Parameshwara Shetty that the police have obtained his signature when he was upset due to the death of his daughter.

He and also other witnesses PW.2, P.W.3,
P.W.8 does not know actual reason for committing of suicide by the deceased.

According to the said witnesses, the accused persons never and ever given any sort of torture to the deceased to bring additional dowry and because of the continuous torture deceased has committed suicide.

As such,
learned PP has treated the said witnesses P.W.1 to P.W.3 and P.W.6 as hostile and cross-examined,
but failed to get any useful evidence to believe the allegations made against the accused persons.
As such, the evidence of the above said witnesses not at all helpful for the prosecution to prove the guilt against the accused.
11. The witness Vinod and Arasu examined as P.W.4 and P.W.5 are the signatories to the Mahazar marked at Ex.P.3.
The witness P.W.4 not supported the conducting of Mahazar by the Investigation Officer by becoming hostile.
Even in the cross-examination of learned PP failed to support the prosecution case by giving positive evidence according to the recitals of Mahazar Ex.P.3.

Whereas the witness P.W.5 has specifically deposed that police have seized the death note, one book,
marriage invitation at the place of incident.
His signature present in the Mahazar marked at Ex.P.3 and seized tissue paper box marked at M.O.1.
Even though he has supported the conducting of Mahazar, but the concerned police not submitted the death note and marriage invitation alongwith charge sheet.

However in the cross-examination, said witness has failed to give evidence to show which material object has seized by the police and it is say of the said witness the police have obtained his signatures both at the spot and police station.
He does not know the name of the another pancha.
So also, does not know the contents of the documents to which the police have obtained his signatures in the police station.
So, the entire testimony of the witness P.W.5 is surrounded with doubts.
As already discussed above, non-production of the death note and other documents certainly fatal to the case of the prosecution.

12. The witness P.W.7 Lakshmana has registered FIR vide Cr.No.10/2018 on the basis of the complaint lodged by the complainant on 11.01.2018 at mid night 1.30 a.m and thereafter handed over further investigation to witness C.W.24/P.W.6 S.Prakash, the then ACP.
The FIR has been marked at Ex.P.8 through the witness P.W.7.
The witness P.W.6 after receiving the further investigation has visited the spot and carried out Mahazar at the place of incident and seized tissue packets and marriage invitation.
The said witness evidence is silent so far as death note and the book alleged to be seized by the Investigation Officer as per the version of the pancha.
The said witness prepared the Mahazar as per Ex.P.3 at spot.
The both accused were arrested and produced before the court alongwith the remand application.
He has brought the clothes of the deceased into P.F.No.10/2018 which were collected by the doctor while conducting the post mortem.

4 clothes of the deceased has been marked at M.O.2 to M.O.7.

sentences.text: He has recorded statements of the witnesses on 12.01.2018, received the inquest report and P.M.Report as per Ex.P.6 and Ex.P.7 respectively.
Thereafter as investigation was completed, submitted charge sheet against the accused.
The entire evidence of both the police official witnesses P.W.6 and P.W.7 completely denied by the accused counsel.
So, it is very clear there is no corroboration between the evidence of the witnesses and Investigation Officer.
So, it is very clear that the prosecution has failed to place material iota evidence to establish the guilt against the accused No.2.
Hence, this court has answered the Point Nos.1 and 2 in the Negative.
13. Point No.3:

In view of answer of this court on points No.1 and 2, this court proceed to pass the following:
O R D E R U/s.235(1) of Cr.P.C. the accused No.2 is hereby acquitted of the offences punishable under Sections 498A and 304(B) of IPC.
The bail bond and surety bond of accused No.2 stands cancelled.
The M.O.1 being tissue papers and M.O.2 to M.O.7 being clothes of deceased are being worthless, are ordered to be destroyed after appeal period is over.
